zones.name: The Báb
zones.subtitle: 1819–1850 · the Forerunner
zones.blurb: Siyyid ʻAlí Muhammad, the Báb, who heralded "Him Whom God shall make manifest." His major books have no authorized English translation; the only public-domain access is through Browne and Nicolas.

zones.name: Baháʼuʼlláh
zones.subtitle: 1817–1892 · the Founder
zones.blurb: Mírzá Husayn-ʻAlí, Baháʼuʼlláh. His central works are all in print in authorized English — every one under active copyright, freely readable via the Bahá’í Reference Library.

zones.name: ʻAbduʼl-Bahá
zones.subtitle: 1844–1921 · the Exemplar
zones.blurb: ʻAbbás Effendi, ʻAbduʼl-Bahá — son, successor, and authorized interpreter. His "A Traveller’s Narrative" is the one Bahá’í primary text with a clean public-domain English translation (Browne, 1891).

chips.name: Paris Talks · The Promulgation of Universal Peace

zones.name: Shoghi Effendi & the House of Justice
zones.subtitle: interpretation & legislation
zones.blurb: Shoghi Effendi (d.1957), "the Guardian," authored the interpretive histories and translated most of the canon; the Universal House of Justice (1963– ) is the infallible legislature.

chips.name: God Passes By (1944 — the definitive history)
